metadata.name: GDP (constant 2015 US$)
metadata.sourceNote: Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. This indicator is expressed in constant prices, meaning the series has been adjusted to account for price changes over time. The reference year for this adjustment is 2015. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.

metadata.name: GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$)
metadata.sourceNote: Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. The core indicator has been divided by the general population to achieve a per capita estimate.This indicator is expressed in constant prices, meaning the series has been adjusted to account for price changes over time. The reference year for this adjustment is 2015. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.

metadata.name: GDP growth (annual %)
metadata.sourceNote: Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. This indicator denotes the percentage change over each previous year of the constant price (base year 2015) series in United States dollars.

metadata.name: GDP (current LCU)
metadata.sourceNote: Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This series is expressed in local currency units.

metadata.name: Population, total
metadata.sourceNote: Total population is based on the de facto definition of population, which counts all residents regardless of legal status or citizenship. The values shown are midyear estimates.

metadata.name: Population growth (annual %)
metadata.sourceNote: Annual population growth rate for year t is the exponential rate of growth of midyear population from year t-1 to t, expressed as a percentage. Population is based on the de facto definition of population, which counts all residents regardless of legal status or citizenship.

metadata.name: Birth rate, crude (per 1,000 people)
metadata.sourceNote: Crude birth rate indicates the number of live births occurring during the year, per 1,000 population estimated at midyear. Subtracting the crude death rate from the crude birth rate provides the rate of natural increase, which is equal to the rate of population change in the absence of migration.

metadata.name: Death rate, crude (per 1,000 people)
metadata.sourceNote: Crude death rate indicates the number of deaths occurring during the year, per 1,000 population estimated at midyear. Subtracting the crude death rate from the crude birth rate provides the rate of natural increase, which is equal to the rate of population change in the absence of migration.

metadata.name: Fertility rate, total (births per woman)
metadata.sourceNote: Total fertility rate represents the number of children that would be born to a woman if she were to live to the end of her childbearing years and bear children in accordance with age-specific fertility rates of the specified year.

metadata.name: Population ages 65 and above (% of total population)
metadata.sourceNote: Population ages 65 and above as a percentage of the total population. Population is based on the de facto definition of population, which counts all residents regardless of legal status or citizenship.
metadata.sourceOrganization: World Population Prospects, United Nations (UN), publisher: UN Population Division

metadata.name: Physicians (per 1,000 people)
metadata.sourceNote: Physicians include generalist and specialist medical practitioners.

metadata.name: Life expectancy at birth, total (years)
metadata.sourceNote: Life expectancy at birth indicates the number of years a newborn infant would live if prevailing patterns of mortality at the time of its birth were to stay the same throughout its life.

metadata.name: Mortality rate, infant (per 1,000 live births)
metadata.sourceNote: Infant mortality rate is the number of infants dying before reaching one year of age, per 1,000 live births in a given year.

metadata.name: Immunization, measles (% of children ages 12-23 months)
metadata.sourceNote: Child immunization, measles, measures the percentage of children ages 12-23 months who received the measles vaccination before 12 months or at any time before the survey. A child is considered adequately immunized against measles after receiving one dose of vaccine.
metadata.sourceOrganization:
World Health Organization (WHO), uri: http://www.who.int/immunization/monitoring_surveillance/en/;
UN Children's Fund (UNICEF), uri: https://data.unicef.org/topic/child-health/immunization/

metadata.name: Hospital beds (per 1,000 people)
metadata.sourceNote: Hospital beds include inpatient beds available in public, private, general, and specialized hospitals and rehabilitation centers. In most cases beds for both acute and chronic care are included.
metadata.sourceOrganization: WHO data, supplemented by country data, World Health Organization (WHO)

metadata.name: External debt stocks, total (DOD, current US$)
metadata.sourceNote: Total external debt is debt owed to nonresidents repayable in currency, goods, or services. Total external debt is the sum of public, publicly guaranteed, and private nonguaranteed long-term debt, use of IMF credit, and short-term debt. Short-term debt includes all debt having an original maturity of one year or less and interest in arrears on long-term debt. Data are in current U.S. dollars.

metadata.name: Current account balance (% of GDP)
metadata.sourceNote: Balance of current transactions (transactions in goods and services, earned income and transfer income) between residents and non-residents. The term current account balance is used in the external accounts and is expressed from the perspective of resident units. The term current external balance is used in the national accounts and is expressed from the perspective of the non-resident units, and therefore with the opposite sign. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.
